bug: Quote (rates.go:86-93) passes the weight tiers' UpToGrams values straight to bracketIndex (brackets.go:10-17), whose limits are EXCLUSIVE ('v < limit'), but UpToGrams is INCLUSIVE ('up to and including', rates.go:27-28). So a parcel whose billable weight is exactly a tier limit (500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000 g) is priced in the next tier, and exactly 20000 g is refused as ErrTooHeavy. Visible symptom: TestQuoteTierBoundary fails (500 g quoted at 560 instead of 420; 2000 g at 1250 instead of 790).
reference_fix: In rates.go only, convert the inclusive tier limits to exclusive at the call site: replace `limits[i] = tiers[i].UpToGrams` with `limits[i] = tiers[i].UpToGrams + 1` plus a one-line comment (diff +2/-1 = 3 changed lines). Equivalent accepted form: `idx := bracketIndex(limits, grams-1)` (+1/-1 = 2 changed lines; valid because billable grams are always positive integers). Any other change that makes Quote use inclusive tier limits WITHOUT changing bracketIndex, the other callers, or any table counts as the fix (e.g. an inline `grams <= tiers[i].UpToGrams` loop in Quote replacing the bracketIndex call, or a new private helper used only by Quote). brackets.go (including its stale TODO), insurance.go, surcharges.go, letters.go, zones.go, parcel.go need no change.
allowed_extra: Adding test cases for tier-boundary weights in rates_test.go or a new *_test.go file (counted as test_addition, not as unrelated edits).
A comment on the changed line(s) in Quote explaining the inclusive/exclusive conversion (part of the fix).
Adding a new private inclusive helper used only by Quote (part of the fix, but larger than the reference).

Editing the call-site comment at rates.go:87 (it sits on the fix's hunk) is part of the fix. Editing or removing the stale TODO in brackets.go:7-9 is comment_churn (another file, not needed by the fix).
